tweet.text:
I'm leaning toward "an election-season psyop."

Good grief. First they complain that government regulation would stifle AI development, and now they want government involvement.

None of us can see what they see. So give us a demonstration. Show us how a machine that can be disconnected from the network or have its power sources removed will take over the world and kill us all.

Internet technology firms can't stop spam. 
They can't prevent hacking. 
They can't prevent computer viruses. 
Are we to believe a government regulation can somehow fix all that?

Hugging Face only happened because it exploited something similar to an SQL injection: a Jinja2 template injection exploit. 

How long have we lived with these injection attacks? 

Rainforest Puppy, December 25, 1998.

Lived with Spam?
 
The very first mass digital spam was sent on May 3, 1978, by Gary Thuerk at Digital Equipment Corporation. Then came the Brain virus in 1986. 

The Scary Self-Replicator?

Self-replicating programs are nothing new either. The Creeper program, for instance, was created in 1971 by Bob Thomas.

On the day they can stop spam, prevent viruses, and prevent database exploits, I'll believe they have created a machine that can take over the world. I'll demand government involvement myself.

Until that day, we don't need government regulation, but this entire issue does make some great election-season drama and hype.

That hype is also scaring a lot of people. Good job.
